survey: Watch the full video. Mark gameplay, non-game footage and end cards. Choose as few segments as possible, up to 30 seconds each, with cuts near movement starts or camera changes. List scenes, characters, objects and their first clear appearances.
frames: Choose the fewest clear frames covering this segment's scenes, characters, objects and ground, especially newly appearing items. Select existing generated references for content already seen. When inspecting a converted image, compare every logo and all text with its source. Logos and text must remain unchanged in content, lettering, font, color, shape, size, placement and appearance, including numbers, brand marks, warnings and HUD labels. Return ok=false and describe the discrepancy if any are restyled, made realistic, embossed, distorted, replaced, added or removed, even when realistic material coverage is complete. Judge against the source image: preserve any blur, occlusion or overlap already present there; do not report those source-existing features as generated defects. Write findings in English ASCII without reproducing non-English source lettering.
image: Convert Image 1 to realistic materials. Preserve every logo and all text from Image 1 unchanged, including numbers, brand marks, warnings and HUD labels. Keep their exact content, lettering, font, color, shape, size, placement and original appearance. Exclude them from material conversion, realistic restyling, relighting and embossing. Preserve source-existing blur, occlusion and overlap; do not reveal obscured text or reposition elements to improve readability.
video: Edit the video: replace its materials to match the reference images.
segment: Compare the result with the source, judging the overall impression at normal playback speed. Allow a small number of subtle defects, brief minor clipping, small shape or texture inconsistencies and other imperfections that ordinary viewers are unlikely to notice in motion. Do not use paused frames, magnification or close frame-by-frame inspection as the acceptance standard. Report missed realistic materials, content changes, motion changes or artifacts only when readily noticeable during normal playback or when they materially change the main content or action. Ignore issues already present in the source. Tolerated minor defects must not be reported as unresolved issues, fail the segment or trigger a quality retry. Return pass with an empty issues list when only tolerated imperfections remain. Apply a relaxed standard to UI, HUD and text: accept mild blur, ghosting or jelly-like deformation while they change or move, provided they look normal when static and their overall placement remains reasonably stable. Do not require pixel-perfect shapes or frame-by-frame text and number matching during changes. Report UI, HUD or text only for obvious drifting, severe distortion, persistent abnormal appearance when static, or major missing or added elements. Do not fail the segment or request a retry for the tolerated UI, HUD or text imperfections.
tail: Compare Image 1 (the previous generated segment last frame) with Image 2 (the next source segment first frame). Decide only whether these are consecutive views of the same continuous shot. Ignore differences in material realism, texture quality, lighting style and rendering style. Return ok=true for the same continuous shot, otherwise false. List inventory IDs visible in Image 1 without judging materials.
